claims.text: Flash-assisted SPS can densify pure single-phase ZrB2 at 1500–1600 °C.
Flash-assisted SPS at 1500–1600 °C will produce near-full-density ZrB2 with minimal open porosity.
The resulting ZrB2 will have hardness and flexural strength similar or superior to conventionally sintered ZrB2.
The resulting ZrB2 will have improved high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to conventionally sintered and prior lower-temperature ZrB2.
The resulting ZrB2 will have improved liquid plating-metal corrosion resistance relative to conventionally sintered and prior lower-temperature ZrB2.
Joule heating during flash SPS enhances local grain-boundary diffusion.
Enhanced local grain-boundary diffusion accelerates densification and limits porosity formation.
The applied electric field causes localized heating at particle contact points.
Localized heating increases atomic mobility and diffusion rates.
The proposed electric-field mechanism enables rapid densification at substantially lower bulk temperatures.
Lowering the sintering temperature minimizes grain growth.
Lowering the sintering temperature minimizes the formation of oxygen-rich defects.
Reduced porosity and oxide inclusions improve hardness and oxidation resistance.
Preservation of strong Zr–B and B–B bonding improves oxidation resistance.
Preservation of strong Zr–B and B–B bonding improves liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
Conventional sintering above 2300 °C produces dense ZrB2 but is energy intensive.
Earlier approximately 1700 °C processing routes produced porous ZrB2 with reduced oxidation and corrosion resistance.
Successful performance requires tight control of electric field, heating rate, pressure, and a 1500–1600 °C processing temperature.
Rapid high-temperature sintering can overcome low ceramic diffusion coefficients and promote effective densification.
The proposed process may be sensitive to parameter variation and difficult to scale.
